title: VehicleSetupCompletionResponse
description: The 200 body of POST /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/complete-setup (rest-api.md §7.23, contracts v0.25.0) — the ACTION half of the setupState surfaces MYR-491 put on §7.0 and §7.1. WHY IT IS A SEPARATE SCHEMA AND NOT A REUSE: the object is the same shape, but the CONTRACT AROUND IT is deliberately stronger in two ways that a shared schema could not express. (1) `setupState` here is NEVER null — a passive read may make no claim, but a request that asked the server to finish setting up a car always gets an answer, and null would be useless to the client rendering the progress card. (2) The `state` enum is a SUPERSET: it carries `streaming`, the positive member §7.0/§7.1 deliberately lack (MYR-491: 'null is NOT ready — there is no ready member'), because on this surface the server has just looked at the car's status and freshness and does know. THE SERVER NEVER EMITS `streaming` ON §7.0 OR §7.1, and a consumer must not expect it there. Every other member means exactly what it means on the read surfaces, produced by the same server-side helpers, so the two can never disagree about one vehicle. FAILURE IS NEVER A STATE: every way this endpoint can fail is a typed HTTP error (§7.23's table) and no error response carries a setupState at all, so a client renders a retry affordance from the code rather than a setup card. SHARED WITH §7.24 (MYR-599, contracts v0.39.0): `POST /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/acknowledge-owner-approval` returns THIS SAME SHAPE, deliberately, so a client reuses its existing completion handling verbatim — record the acknowledgment, run the same best-effort config push complete-setup runs, answer with the vehicle's resulting setupState. See `$defs.AcknowledgeOwnerApprovalRequest` for that endpoint's request body and its full contract.

vehicleId.description: The Prisma cuid the request addressed, echoed back so a client completing several vehicles can attribute each answer. NOT a VIN — a full VIN never crosses this wire (§1.3, §2.1).

setupState.description: What now stands between this vehicle and live telemetry, as of this request. NEVER null on this surface — contrast VehicleState.setupState / VehicleSummary.setupState, where null is the ordinary 'no claim' answer. Same two members and the same semantics; one shared server-side derivation, so a completion response and the next snapshot cannot contradict each other.

state.description: `streaming` — the car is sending live telemetry; setup is COMPLETE and nothing further is required. THIS MEMBER IS EXCLUSIVE TO §7.23/§7.24 and is never emitted on §7.0/§7.1. `awaiting_owner_acknowledgment` (MYR-599, contracts v0.39.0) — the car was linked by someone holding DRIVER access on Tesla's side and the owner-approval acknowledgment has NOT been recorded, so the server refused to push a telemetry config and is telling the client what is missing rather than inventing progress. THE LINKER MUST ACT: present the acknowledgment sheet and POST §7.24. Reachable from §7.23 as well as §7.24 — complete-setup on an unacknowledged driver car returns this state instead of pushing — and it SORTS BEFORE `configuring` / `awaiting_virtual_key` / `token_failed`, because consent precedes pairing evidence and no push has been attempted. From §7.24 it is the answer to a call whose acknowledgment did not stick; the ordinary §7.24 answer is the NEXT state (usually `awaiting_virtual_key` or `configuring`). `configuring` — the virtual key is confirmed enrolled and the fleet-telemetry config has been pushed, either by this call or earlier in the same pairing epoch; NO OWNER ACTION, the client narrates progress and may suggest waking the car's screen if it persists. `awaiting_virtual_key` — Tesla reports the virtual key is NOT enrolled on the vehicle; THE OWNER MUST ACT, and because the client knows it just sent them to the Tesla app it should surface the pairing retry proactively rather than leaving them to discover a dead control (MYR-503). `token_failed` — the owner's Tesla authorization can no longer be resolved or refreshed; THE OWNER MUST ACT (reconnect the Tesla account). NOTE WHAT IS ABSENT: there is no member for 'we could not tell'. A car whose pairing Tesla would not report, a car that would not wake, and a config push that failed are all typed HTTP errors, because a confident wrong answer on a card whose job is naming the ONE thing left to do is worse than no answer. New members may be added in a minor version; consumers MUST treat an unrecognised value as 'setup is incomplete, reason unknown' and MUST NOT fail the decode.

since.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant at which the evidence behind `state` was recorded — the last live frame for `streaming`, the forced re-push or the pairing epoch it belongs to for `configuring`, and this read for `awaiting_virtual_key` / `token_failed`. It is DATA FOR THE COPY ('for 2 minutes'), NOT an input a consumer re-derives `state` from. Never zero and never in the future: the server floors it at the read instant, so a client may subtract it from `now` without guarding for a negative age.

AcknowledgeOwnerApprovalRequest.title: AcknowledgeOwnerApprovalRequest
AcknowledgeOwnerApprovalRequest.description: The request body of `POST /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/acknowledge-owner-approval` (rest-api.md §7.24, MYR-599, contracts v0.39.0) — the consent gate in front of provisioning a car its linker DRIVES but does not OWN on Tesla's side. WHY THE ENDPOINT EXISTS: a driver-access vehicle IS provisioned (the row is created, the virtual key the person already paired is not wasted), but NOTHING is pushed to the car — no fleet-telemetry config, no reconnect, no keepalive re-push — until the person who linked it states that the owner approved adding it. The vehicle reads `setupState.state` = 'awaiting_owner_acknowledgment' and `teslaAccessType` = 'driver' until then. AUTH AND OWNERSHIP: bearer, and the caller must own the platform's Vehicle row — the SAME ownership check as §7.23 complete-setup, with the SAME answer when it fails: 404 `not_found`, never 403, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which vehicleIds exist. IDEMPOTENT BY DESIGN: a second call on an already-acknowledged car is a 200, never a 409 — it re-runs the same best-effort config push and returns the vehicle's current setupState, which makes it a safe retry for a client that lost the first response, and a usable 'try again' for a push that failed transiently. The stored acknowledgment is NOT overwritten into something weaker: the first acknowledgment's instant is what the platform would point to if an owner ever complained. OWNER-ACCESS CARS ARE A 200 NO-OP: a vehicle whose `teslaAccessType` is 'owner' has nothing to acknowledge, so the call records nothing, pushes nothing new and returns the setupState the normal derivation yields — a client that cannot tell the two cases apart is never punished for asking. RESPONSE: VehicleSetupCompletionResponse, the SAME shape §7.23 returns (`vehicleId`, non-null `setupState`), so the client's existing completion handling is reused unchanged — usually `awaiting_virtual_key` next, and the existing pair-key card takes over. FAILURE IS NEVER A STATE, exactly as on §7.23: every way this can fail is a typed HTTP error and no error body carries a setupState.

acknowledgmentVersion.description: The version id of the acknowledgment text the client ACTUALLY RENDERED, verbatim, on the sheet the person confirmed. The canonical text and its id ship with this contracts package (`owner-approval-v1`); a client MUST send the id of the copy it displayed and MUST NOT invent, abbreviate or re-word one — the whole point of storing it is that the platform can later say WHICH words a person agreed to. The server stores this string and the instant, and NOTHING ELSE about the acknowledgment; it does not validate the text, only that the id is present and within length. An id the server does not recognise is still recorded as sent, because a client shipped before a copy revision must not be blocked from finishing setup. Format is a lowercase slug with a version suffix; treat it as an OPAQUE token, never parse it for ordering. P0: a consent-record version marker, carrying no personal data — the person is identified by the authenticated caller, not by anything in this body.
